This Tuned Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren Will Annoy Purists. But It’s Not Real
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | onb.artdesign
Every gearhead and their grandmother will recognize the Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren in a sea of supercars, and that’s despite the fact that this exotic model hasn’t been a thing since 2010.
Production spanned from 2003 to 2010, and it is estimated that over 2,000 examples saw the light of day during this time. All of them were made at McLaren’s factory in Woking, UK. Gordon Murray and Gorden Wagener were responsible with the design, and the model was offered as a two-door coupe and a two-door roadster. The speedster (Stirling Moss) joined them, and all had a front mid-engine and rear-wheel drive layout.
Due to the layout, the Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren is more of an exotic grand tourer rather than a full-blown supercar, but it’s definitely not wrong to refer to it by using the latter term. After all, just look at it! Hasn’t it aged perfectly? It certainly has, this writer thinks, and given the face that it is an automotive icon, purists will be annoyed by the fact that some copies have been visited by the tuning fairy, including the one pictured above.
Or has it? Actually, this is nothing more than a mere rendering take on the model, which features a few modifications. The front bumper is new, and it is bigger than the OEM one. It features some flicks, as well as a splitter. The hood has also been tweaked, there is new trim on the front fenders, and we can also see new side skirt attachments.
Photo: Instagram | onb.artdesign Fender flares are part of the CGI makeover, and this Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren also features a new rear bumper, a diffuser, and a giant wing attached to the trunk lid. The ducktail spoiler is also new, and so other other bits and bobs on the outside. The wheels are significantly larger than the OEM ones, and we can see that the tailpipe trim is also on the fresh side of things.
The cockpit hasn’t opened up to the camera, but believe us when we tell you that while it definitely shows its age, it is not bad at all. Some will argue that the quality of materials is on a next level compared to today’s Mercedes cars, but that’s a topic for another time.
Meanwhile, we will wrap it up by reminding you that the Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren features a supercharged 5.4-liter V8 engine, making 617 hp (460 kW/626 ps) in the regular variant, with superior models having 641 hp (478 kW/650 ps) available via the right pedal. A five-speed automatic transmission delivered the power to the rear wheels.
The SLR took around 3.5 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) in independent tests, and could keep pushing up to 208 mph (334 kph). Not bad for a ride that’s more than two decades old, is it? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Onur Bakır (@onb.artdesign)
